jayananda-cm.title: Скорбь Ситы и Адвайты; уход Адвайты в паушу
jayananda-cm.summary: У Ситы и Адвайты в сердце скорбь о Чайтанье и Нитьянанде; через сколько-то дней Адвайта по своей воле говорит, что оставит землю, и в светлый тринадцатый день пауши уходит на Вайкунтху.

verses.text:
У Ситы и Адвайты в сердце осталась великая скорбь:
«Увы, Чайтанья, Нитьянанда Сварупа!»
> Ачарья Госани провёл [ещё] сколько-то дней;
«Я оставлю землю», — сказал он по своей воле.
> В светлый тринадцатый лунный день месяца пауша
Ачарья Госани ушёл на Вайкунтху.
1–2. [= статья Н. Васу 1897 г., краткое жизнеописание Чайтаньи: «Ачарья Госани провёл [ещё] сколько-то дней…» — «…Ачарья Госани ушёл на Вайкунтху».]

verses_en.text:
"First the Lord's birth and deeds are revealed:
in the month of Phalguna Rahu swallowed the moon whole.
> Nimai, Gauranga, and first of all Vishvambhara by name —
these three names are an abode of blessing for the world.
> Seeing on his lotus feet the marks of banner, thunderbolt and goad,
Shachi and Jagannatha Mishra were very happy at heart.
> At six months, as he slept on a bedstead,
a snake held its hood over his head — all the people saw it.
> On the pretext of crying, how much magic he worked!
All the people joyfully said, "Hari, Hari!"
> Every day he played with the children in the middle of the courtyard;
all say: golden anklets ring on his feet.
> Thieves, greedy for wealth, carried him off to kill him;
leading the thieves astray, the Lord came back home.
> [p. 221]
> With the children on the bank of the Ganga, in a little house of sand,
clapping his hands, he revealed kirtana there.
> Striking his mother in the face with a brick,
he gave her tulasi buds, proclaiming bhakti.*
> Day and night Jagadisha in Hiranya's house —
on the day of Hari the Lord ate [their] offering.*
> A brahmana came and offered food to Krishna —
[the Lord,] touching it, ate his rice and curries.
> Sudarshana Pandita put chalk into his hands;
[…] he struck his teacher with a book.*
> When the time came for piercing his ears,
a garland fell from heaven onto the pot of Ganesha.
> Chhaliyadhara,* the king's messenger, was bitten by a snake;
making him say "Krishna," [the Lord] took away his pride.
> Stealing jute from Sridhara,*
he grew headstrong, heeding no one's word.
> From Burana came Sri Haridasa;
he freed the dog Gangadasa from a curse.*
> He fulfilled the desires of all the wives of good families;
soon his elder brother took sannyasa.
> At an auspicious moment the tonsure and the upanayana were performed;
Gauranga took on a form that charms women.
> Expounding the Kalapa, he became a teacher;
in explaining word and meaning, panditas [before him] are herons.*
> Gangadasa Pandita, well known in Navadvipa —
in his house he revealed all learning.
> Merely by discussing the Kalapa he knew everything;
disputing, he taught in Navadvipa.
> Mishra Purandara departed to Vaikuntha;
handsome Gauranga married Lakshmi.
> In every sutra he expounded devotion to Vishnu;
no one had the power to understand that exposition.
> Then the Lord defeated the conqueror of the quarters*
and at last destroyed all his bonds.
> Telling Gadadhara and Srinivasa in particular,
on the pretext of earning money he went to Vanga.
> The eastern land, Vanga, then became a tirtha;
by a snakebite mother Lakshmi* went to Vaikuntha.
> Returning from Vanga, marrying Vishnupriya,
he roams joyfully about the city of Nadia.
> When his father died,* going to Gaya, he saw Ishvara Puri;
staying on the Rajagiri hill, [he] showed him grace.
> With water that had washed the feet of brahmanas he removed the burden of sins;
the lord of munis, Madhavendra Puri, sees the six-armed form in the matha.*
> At Gayashira he offered pindas at Vishnu's footprint
and delivered all his ancestors one by one.
> In Gaya Gauranga's glory grew greatly:
by the touch of his feet a stone image was set free.
> An old brahmana woman gave him water that had washed [his] feet —
drinking the foot-water, the old woman vanished.*
> Returning from Gaya, in Srinivasa's house
he had kunda flowers gathered every evening.
> Then for some days he was seized by "wind";*
he revealed all the prema-bhakti there is.
> In Srinivasa's house, on Vishnu's throne,*
the Lord revealed himself in the sight of all.
> Nityananda Gosani left Varanasi;
hearing of Gauranga's glory, he came to Navadvipa.
> He showed the six-armed form to Nityananda Svarupa,
[who] stayed in the house of Nandana Acharya in Navadvipa.
> He showed the Boar form to Murari Gupta;
mounting his shoulders, he showed grace to the son of a maidservant.*
> In ecstasy Gaurachandra became the Haladhara;
Nityananda put plough and pestle into his hands.
> [p. 222]
> When the time of the shraddha of Srinivasa's father drew near […].*
> At mealtime the Lord's hair came loose;
becoming four-armed, he tied it up with two hands.
> Nityananda, on the pretext of the Vyasa-puja, broke his staff;
Gauranga, with a leap, falls into the water of the Ganga.
> He freed Jagai and Madhai from great sin,
the two robber brothers Dhubalia and Sindhalia.*
> Breaking the Kazi's house in the village of Simulia,*
in the "seven-watch" ecstasy* he was full of joy.
> In every house in Navadvipa, Hari-sankirtana;
the yavanas fled, leaving the village of Simulia.
> Shuklambara Brahmachari's bag of alms
[the Lord] snatched and ate from; the brahmana was dismayed.
> Dancing in sankirtana, he took on the mood of Rukmini;
he gave the breast to all the Vaishnavas.
> All the Vaishnavas see the Lord's various forms;
praising him, all received boons one by one.
> Haridasa received Gauranga's remnants;
[the Lord] drank water from Sridhara's broken iron pot.
> Taking all the companions, together with Nityananda,
he went to Advaita's house, in various delights.
> In Srinivasa's house the Lord dances in sankirtana,
offering everyone the wealth of Vaikuntha — prema.
> Srinivasa's dead son speaks of the truth of the soul;
the grief for his son went far away; [Srinivasa] remains in sankirtana.
> Great was Gauranga's favour to Srinivasa:
at Gauranga's words he forgot his grief for his son.
> […] carried baskets and dhotis for everyone;*
he punished Devananda Pandita.
> All the companions who were in various lands
then came to Navadvipa and gathered together.
> He mocked the great students with a shloka;
the people of Navadvipa could not recognise him.
> Performing bali, vaishvadeva, shraddha — the observances of a brahmana —
[he showed such] purity that Navadvipa marvelled.
> Chaitanya saw the land of his fathers, Jayapura;
he showed great mercy to the maidservant Duhkhi.*
> Through the mouth of Narayani, Srinivasa's niece,
making her say "Hari," he made her weep in the joy of prema.
> As he danced in kirtana, "wind" arose in the Lord;
an exorcist, tying the Lord's feet with a rope, held him.
> The king's man came, seized [someone] and takes him away;
the Lord makes him say "Hari" and weep.*
> In the son of Acharya Gosani, Sri Achyutananda,
Gaurachandra revealed himself — in his body.
> Haridasa Thakura receives the remnants from the Lord's plate,
and only Narayani eats the rest of the remnants.
> In renunciation he revealed the truth to all;
he consoled Vishnupriya with tales of itihasa.
> Leaving the happy household life in Navadvipa,
he revealed himself at Katwa on the bank of the Jahnavi.
> In sannyasa he took the name Sri Krishna-Chaitanya;
seeing him, the people of the world say, "Blessed, blessed!"
> Keshava Bharati, seeing and hearing of the four-armed [form], […];
Nityananda, turning back, threw away the books of the agamas.*
> Vakreshvara, having set out, turned back again;
[the Lord] stayed twelve days in Shantipur.
> Nityananda ran on ahead to Nilachala;
[the Lord] stayed in seclusion; no one could see him.
> Consoling Advaita, he went to Nilachala,
wandering from land to land, from forest to forest.
> Kashi Mishra's house, the Tota — a delightful place:
by Jagannatha's command he took up residence there.
> [p. 223]
> With Sarvabhauma there was a discussion of Vedanta;
hearing [his] arguments,* Sarvabhauma marvelled.
> He showed Sarvabhauma the six-armed form;
Vidya-vachaspati saw the three strides in the Kshetra.*
> Paramananda Puri Gosani met [him] at Setu-bandha;
[the Lord] showed great grace to Raya Ramananda.
> King Prataparudra saw the eight-armed [form];
[the Lord] placed his lotus feet on Vaninatha Pattanayaka.
> […] grace only to Pradyumna […]* —
in his lap Chaitanya Gosani fell asleep.
> Vishnu Puri, Damodara, Vishveshvara,
Govinda and Govindananda — ever with him.
> By Jagannatha's command, in special bliss,
setting out for Mathura, he entered the land of Gauda.
> He stayed in seclusion in the house of Vidya-vachaspati;
all the people, going round the town, saw him.
> With many companions, in special bliss,
he sent Nityananda Svarupa to the land of Gauda.
> On the way Sri Ramadasa is in the divine mood:
people see [him] thrice-bent with a flute and are afraid.
> With a basket of curds on his head, Gadadhara Dasa
in the middle of the road revealed the mood of Radha.
> Parameshvara Dasa entered the divine mood;
Purandara Pandita is drunk with the mood of Angada.*
> Uprooting a tree, he climbs onto the branches of a tree;
someone, rolling over, falls from the roof of a house.
> Raghunatha Vaidya Upadhyaya, the great-minded —
he became like [Nityananda] in Nityananda's mood.
> For three months [Nityananda] was beside himself, at his own will,
in Raghava Pandita's house in the village of Panihati.
> Sri Ramadasa, laughing in the mood of Krishna —
kadamba flowers blossomed on a lime tree.*
> Gadadhara Dasa makes everyone dance in his house;
the singer Madhava Ghosha sings the Dana-khanda.*
> Nityananda makes the Kazi say "Hari bol";
Murari Chaitanyadasa has a quarrel with Raghava.
> He stays submerged in the water for five or seven days;
a black snake bites him — blood flows from his body.
> At Saptagrama Nityananda, in a merchant's house,
dances day and night at a great festival.
> Gold, silver, diamonds, pearls, anklets,
a profusion of lovely painted silks.
> At Shantipur, in Advaita's house, Nityananda
roams at will with Achyutananda.
> At Navadvipa, in Hiranya's house, Nityananda —
a robber brahmana went at night to murder him.
> The night passed; the robber fled in fear:
in storm, rain and darkness he went blind.
> Showing great grace to the robber brahmana,
[Nityananda] sees him floating in tears of prema and thrills.
> In Nilachala the brahmanas and Gauranga remained;
the Lord entrusted the kingdom of Gauda to Nityananda.
> After some days, at the time of the Ratha-yatra, Nityananda
went to Nilachala with all the companions.
> [The Lord] undid the worldly bonds of the Dabir Khas;
to the two brothers he gave the names Rupa and Sanatana.*
> Gaurachandra set out again for Mathura;
Nityananda flooded Gauda with sankirtana.
> Gaurachandra went on pilgrimage to Varanasi
and duly put to shame a heretical sannyasi.
> He went to Prayaga and bathed [at] Veni-Madhava;
at Ayodhya, the Sarayu, the Gharghara, the place of sacrifice.
> Leaving Dvar,* the Lord went quickly
by many difficult roads to Mathura.
> [p. 224]
> He saw at Mathura Madanamohana,
the Kalindi, Kadamba-tala, Mount Govardhana.
> Keshi-ghat, Vamshi-vata he saw one by one;
Bhandira, Bahulavana he saw each.
> The birthplace, the Ranga-bhumi, Vishrama-ghat,
Govinda-raya, Bhratri-vata[?], the stone slab.
> By another road, in the land of Trimalla, on the Venkata mountain,
he saw Trimalla-raya, jewels streaming from his head.*
> The leper Garuda Mishra* he cured of his leprosy
and sent him with his wife to Nilachala.
> Mahrat, Sorai, Shiva-Kanchi, Vishnu-Kanchi;
passing through Vijayanagara he went to Viranchi.*
> Crossing the Mahanadi he went to Nilachala
and remained in Nilachala twenty-eight years.
> All people became righteous, the earth was blessed;
he made a flood of prema reaching to Hemasetu.*
> In the ocean of prema, with Nityananda at the helm,
the cargo of Kali's sins sank in the deep.
> Yama's abode became empty, [and] the torments of hell;
Yama went to Brahma to take counsel.
> Yama says: "Brahma, relieve me of my office:
Sri Chaitanya Thakura has delivered all the sinners.
> All the eighty-four pits of hell have become empty;
sixty thousand messengers sit idle at home.
> Some sinners Sri Jagannatha delivered,
some sinners were freed by the rice of mahaprasada;
> some sinners were freed by serving tulasi,
some sinners were freed by the Ganga and Varanasi;
> some sinners were freed by the shalagrama stone,
some, some sinners were freed by Hari-nama.
> Yama's abode has become empty; there are no more sinners."
Hearing Yama's words, Brahma laughs right there.
> With Indra and Shankara he set out himself;
all the gods together raise cries of victory.
> In Nilachala, at night, Chaitanya in the Tota ashrama
announced in due order that he would go to Vaikuntha:
> "Having agreed on the bright seventh lunar day of Ashadha,
send a chariot — I will go to the city of Vaikuntha."
> Nityananda came [to Nilachala] near the time of the Ratha-yatra;
[the Lord] told Advaita-chandra everything without reserve:
> "Nityananda and Advaita are not different, one form;
not understanding this, people speak of a quarrel.
> I entrust Nityananda to Advaita:
all the sacrifice of sankirtana is in your charge.
> Twenty-eight years* I have stayed in Nilachala;
I shall go to another place — I tell you without reserve.
> There will be many Vaishnavas and many Vaishnavis;
servants and servants of servants will fill the earth.
> The master of this house is Pandita Gosani;
there is no one dearer to me than he."
> Sri Haridasa Thakura stayed in Nilachala;
[the Lord] had a garden-retreat built for him by the sea.
> With many servants, in joy, Nityananda
Gaurachandra sent to the land of Gauda.
> In Ashadha Prataparudra sits in the Lord's house;
Advaita, smiling, speaks of Krishna.
> [p. 225]
> Standing, the Lord wets the string of his loincloth […];
"Give my body to the fire […], my life" […].*
> Mahendra Bharati died [by] […] haritaki;*
three hundred yatis put fire in his mouth.
> Haridasa Thakura departed first,
on the bright fourteenth day of Phalguna.
> In Ashadha, as he was dancing at the chariot procession,
suddenly a brick struck his left foot.
> Advaita set out at dawn for the land of Gauda;
in private [the Lord] told him something particular there.
> In the waters of Narendra, with all his companions,
Chaitanya sported in the water in many ways.
> On the sixth day the pain in his foot was great;
on that account he at last lay down in the Tota.
> To Pandita Gosani he told everything:
"Tomorrow, at the tenth danda of the night, I shall surely go."
> From somewhere came divine garlands of many colours;
how many vidyadharas dance on the royal road!
> "Bring the chariot, bring the chariot!" the gods call out;
the Lord mounted the chariot with the Garuda banner.
> The illusory body remained lying there;
Chaitanya went to Vaikuntha, leaving Jambudvipa.
> Many servants died of snakebite;
there were meteors, thunderbolts, earthquakes.
> Nityananda and Advaita Acharya Gosani heard;
Vishnupriya and Shachi Thakurani fainted.
> Sri Ramadasa [came] with all the companions;
Nityananda consoled [them], giving them comfort.
> Purushottama and the other companions of Advaita,
hearing of Chaitanya's departure, were struck dumb.
> In separation from Chaitanya, Nityananda constantly
listens to [the tale of] the lila of Chaitanya's departure.
> Nityananda, consoling all the companions,
dances in the bliss of Chaitanya, in the wealth of kirtana:
> "If I bear the name Nityananda Svarupa,
if I do not make Vaishnavas of all, down to the chandala, [—]
> I will make no distinction of caste for chandala or yavana;
giving prema-bhakti to all, I will make them dance in kirtana."
> Sri Ramadasa holds all power:
he will reveal the fifty-six crores of the Yadu line.
> "I will make the wives of good families dance in the bliss of kirtana;
the blind, the deaf and the dull will dance at will.
> I will bring Chaitanya, I will make people accept that Chaitanya;
I will make the kingdoms of Gauda and Utkala blessed, blessed."
> Hearing this vow of Nityananda,
all the Vaishnavas raise the cry, "Glory, glory!"
> After some days Nityananda, wearing the shikha and the sacred thread,
wandered the earth in the guise of a great wrestler.
> The daughters of Suryadasa, Sri Vasu and Jahnava,*
he took in marriage, freely and merrily.
> From Vasu's womb appeared Gosani Virabhadra;
Jahnava's son is Ramabhadra, a great wrestler.*
> Murari Chaitanyadasa catches and brings a tiger;
he sleeps on a bed of snakes — all people know it.
> Sri Sundarananda Thakura, in the water,
catches a crocodile and brings it before everyone.
> Disputing with the Kazi, in the madness of prema,
Gangadasa stayed seven days in a pool of the Ganga.
> Great was the madness of prema of Kamalakara Pippalai:
he cut his own body, and yet he did not come to himself.
> Gadadhara Dasa disputed with the Kazi
and leapt into a pit of fire — seeing it, the people were afraid.
> Purushottama Dasa ate the poison of the mandara*
and digested the poison by the power of the bliss of prema.
> [p. 226]
> As Sanjaya Pandita danced in the mood of a child,
suddenly a snake came out of his mouth.
> In ecstasy Murari Gupta became Hanuman:
a tail came out of him, twelve cubits long.
> Purandara Pandita climbs to the top of a tree;
a sixteen-cubit tail hangs down to the foot of the tree.
> Parameshvara Dasa ate three measures* of earth;
Balarama Dasa burns [the dwellings?] of the yavanas.*
> Kaliya Krishnadasa binds and brings a crocodile;
seeing it, Sri Nityananda's delight increased.
> Sri Nityananda made his home at Khardaha,
where the line of the great kulina Yogeshvara lives.*
> Advaita-chandra's line dwells in Shantipur:
the sons and grandsons of Sita and Advaita appear.
> Sankirtana and temples will be in every kingdom:
[by this] weighty deed he removed the earth's burden.
> The treasure of Chaitanya's life is Lord Nityananda:
not for an instant did he see [him] in separation, as if he were blind.*
> Nityananda always stays at home;
Gauridasa Pandita gives him help.
> Gauridasa Pandita — the four brothers together —
with Nityananda merrily carry on the dhamali of rapture.
> Thousands upon thousands — so many servants of Advaita!
Their servants fill the world.
> The servants of Chaitanya are without limit;
the servants of Nityananda have great prosperity.
> All the servants who are with Nityananda-chandra
I could not tell in a thousand years.
> Each servant has a following of thousands upon thousands;
by Nityananda's grace they are like Krishna.
> In the Kali age the world became righteous;
all the heavy burden of the earth was removed.
> Nityananda said to Gauridasa Pandita:
"[…] Pandita, I remain on this earth."*
> In the month of Ashvina, at a conjunction, on the dark eighth lunar day,
Nityananda went to Vaikuntha, leaving the earth.
> On the day of Ekadashi it was like the dissolution of the world:
at the breath of Ananta the earth trembled.
> The mahantas who heard of Nityananda's departure,
seeing Virabhadra, were wholly comforted.
> Sita and Advaita were left with great grief in their hearts:
"Alas, Chaitanya, Nityananda Svarupa!"
> Acharya Gosani passed some more days;
"I shall leave the earth," he said of his own accord.
> On the bright thirteenth lunar day of the month of Pausha
Acharya Gosani departed to Vaikuntha.
> Svasti! Glory, glory to the Chaitanya-mangala,
the crest-jewel of avataras, in which all is revealed!
> Whoever sings of Chaitanya, or makes others sing of Chaitanya,
is Chaitanya's servant, and Chaitanya is his helper.
> To his sons, grandsons, great-grandsons and all the rest
Jayananda's blessing: the fulfilment of their wishes.
> Meditating on the two feet of Chaitanya and Gadadhara,
Jayananda joyfully sings the Uttara-khanda." The end.
notes: "রুধিআ মাএর মুখে ইটাল মারিঞা" — the sense is conjectural.
Hari-vasara — the Ekadashi day; the episode meant is the one in which the child Nimai demanded and ate the food prepared as an offering to Vishnu in the house of Jagadisha and Hiranya.
"চৈতন্যেতে গুরুতে মারিল পুথির বাড়ি" — the beginning of the line is unclear.
"ছালিয়াধরা" — the name (or nickname) is unidentified; the reading follows the OCR.
"পাটুআ" — jute (or jute leaves eaten as a vegetable); Sridhara is the poor trader with whom, according to the biographies, Nimai bargained in the market.
"সাপে মুক্ত করিল কুকুর গঙ্গাদাস" — the sense is unclear (taken as "শাপে মুক্ত," "freed from a curse").
"পণ্ডিত হএ বক," literally "panditas become herons," i.e. apparently they fall dumb or look foolish; the sense is conjectural.
A digvijayi, "conqueror of the quarters," is a wandering scholar who defeated all comers in debate.
I.e. Lakshmipriya, Chaitanya's first wife.
"বাপ মরিতে গয়া যাইতে" — the journey to Gaya for the funeral rite for his father; Rajagiri (Rajgir) — hills near Gaya.
The connection of the line with its context is unclear: Madhavendra Puri was the guru of Ishvara Puri.
"বুড়ি," an old woman; the episode is known only from Jayananda.
"বায়ু," "wind," i.e. a disorder of the wind (vata) in the body — an illness taken for madness.
"বিষ্ণুখট্টা," the seat (couch) of Vishnu, i.e. the throne of the deity.
"দাসী-পুত্র," "son of a maidservant"; who is meant is unclear (perhaps Murari himself, so naming himself in humility).
The second line of this couplet is missing in the OCR.
"ধুবালিআ সিন্ধালিআ" — apparently nicknames of Jagai and Madhai; the reading follows the OCR.
The OCR has "নিশ্বলিয়া," "লিমলিয়া"; according to the biographies, the Kazi's house stood at Simulia (সিমুলিয়া) near Navadvipa.
"সাত-প্রহরিয়া ভাব," the ecstasy of "seven watches," i.e. the great manifestation (mahaprakasha) that lasted twenty-one hours.
"ভক্ত করি সভার বহিল সাজি ধুতি" — the sense is unclear.
"দুখী দাসী" may also be taken as a name: Duhkhi was a maidservant in Srivasa's house.
Whom the king's man seized is not clear from the text.
"আগম পুথি," the books of the agamas (tantras); perhaps Nityananda's abandonment of earlier rites is meant. The first line of the couplet is incomplete.
"উদ্‌গ্রাহ" — an argument or rejoinder in learned debate; cf. above, the section on language, word 9.
"ত্রিপাদ" — apparently the form of Trivikrama, who covered the worlds in three strides. The Kshetra is Puri.
"রদ্ক অনুগ্রহ মাত্র প্রদ্যুম্ন কানাঞি" — the line is corrupt (perhaps it concerns Pradyumna Mishra or Kanu).
Angada — one of the monkey leaders in the Ramayana.
"জম্বীর" — the lime (citron) tree.
Dana-khanda — songs about Krishna exacting "toll" from the gopis.
Dabir Khas and Sakar Malik — the court titles of Rupa and Sanatana in the service of the sultan of Gauda.
"দ্বার ছাড়ি" — perhaps Haridvar; the sense is conjectural.
Trimalla-raya — the deity on the Venkata hill (Tirumala, Venkateshvara); the second half of the line is unclear.
"কুড়িয়া গরুড়মিশ্র" — the reading follows the OCR; the person is unidentified.
Mahrat, Sorai, Viranchi — readings follow the OCR; the places are unidentified.
"হেমসেতু" — the sense is unclear (perhaps "as far as the Setu," i.e. the southern tip of India).

Vasu's note. According to Krishnadasa Kaviraja, [Chaitanya] lived twenty-four years as a householder and twenty-four years as a sannyasi in Nilachala. But according to Jayananda, Gauranga took sannyasa in his twentieth year, thus: "Fourth, the Sannyasa-khanda — listen with one mind — how [he took] sannyasa and the name Sri Krishna-Chaitanya. Young in years was Gaurachandra, twenty years old; a man of great renunciation, his body pure gold."
The couplet is corrupt ("দাঁড়াএ প্রভুর তিতে কৌপীনের ডোর। অগ্নি দেহ অন্য কনাএ কুঞ্জ প্রাণ মোর"); the rendering is a guess.
"হরিতকী কাষ্ঠে" — the sense is unclear; Mahendra Bharati is unidentified.
The OCR has "শ্রীবস্থ জানকী"; below it has "জাহ্নবীনন্দন," so we read "Jahnava." These are Vasudha and Jahnava, Nityananda's wives.
"জাহ্নবীনন্দন রামভদ্র মহামল্ল" — so in the text; cf. what is known of Ramachandra, Jahnava's adopted son.
"মণ্ডর বিষ" — reading and sense unclear.
"আড়ি" — a measure of grain.
"জবনের সাড়ি" — the sense is unclear.
I.e. the line to which Suryadasa, Nityananda's father-in-law, belonged.
The line is unclear; perhaps "like a blind man [without his guide]."
"নিষ্কপটে পণ্ডিত আমি আছি এই মহী" — the sense is unclear.

verses_en.text: 1–2. [= N. Vasu's article of 1897, the short life of Chaitanya: "Acharya Gosani passed some more days…" — "…Acharya Gosani departed to Vaikuntha."]

prema-vilasa.title: Ещё через два года уходит Адвайта, «отпустив» обоих Прабху; Вриндаван Дас поселяется в Денуре
prema-vilasa.summary: Ещё через два года Адвайта Рай, словно в конце пуджи отпустив обоих Прабху, ушёл в Свою обитель; после ухода трёх Прабху Вриндаван Дас поселился в деревне Денур.

verses.text:
Ещё через два года Шри Адвайта Рай,
отпустив обоих Прабху, ушёл в Свою обитель*.
notes: Образ взят из чина пуджи: Божество «призывают» (авахана) в начале поклонения и «отпускают» (висарджана) в конце; ср. 78.

verses.text:
Призвав, завершив поклонение
и отпустив, Он ушёл в Свою обитель.

После ухода трёх Прабху
Вриндаван поселился в деревне Денур.
Так я вкратце рассказал о Вриндаване Дасе;

verses_en.text:
Two years after that Sri Advaita Raya,
dismissing both Prabhus, went to His own abode.*
notes: The image is taken from the rite of puja: the deity is "invoked" (avahana) at the beginning of worship and "dismissed" (visarjana) at the end; cf. 78.

verses_en.text:
Having invoked, completed the worship,
and dismissed, He went to His own abode.

After the disappearance of the three Prabhus,
Vrindavana settled in the village of Denur.
Thus I have briefly told of Vrindavana Dasa;

advaita-prakasha.title: Сокрытие Адвайты: последний киртан о Гауре; Он входит в храм Мадана-Гопалы и становится невидим
advaita-prakasha.summary: Скорбя, что Его люди хулят Гаурангу, Адвайта решает оставить тело во искупление и созывает Вирачандру, Гауридаса, Нарахари, Кави Карнапуру, Шьямадаса, Вишнудаса, Ядунандану и других; Он велит проповедовать дхарму Чайтаньи и избегать хулителей Гауранги; в киртане семерых плясунов Он в махабхаве восклицает: «Вот Я обрёл Гаурангу!» — входит в храм Мадана-Гопалы и становится невидим; Ачьюта объявляет, что игры Гауранги завершились; по тексту, Адвайта прожил на земле сто двадцать пять лет.

verses.text: Теперь послушайте о сокрытии Шри Адвайты Прабху — когда пишу об этом, разрывается душа.
Однажды Господь впал в великий экстаз и бродил, ища: «Где Нимай?»
Спустя долгое время к Ачарье вернулось внешнее сознание, и Он позвал любимых сыновей.
Господь сказал: «Послушайте, дети, о Моей скорби: Мои злые люди хулят Гаурангу.
Этого Моя душа не может вынести; во искупление этого Я непременно оставлю тело.
Поэтому, передав Моё повеление, приведите сюда любимых преданных Шри Гауранги».
Сказав так, мой Господь оцепенел, а Шри Ачьюта поспешно разослал весть повсюду.
Получив письмо с повелением Господа, Господин Вирачандра пришёл в Шантипур с преданными.
Из Амбики пришёл пандит Гауридас; все преданные Навадвипы пришли к Господу.
С преданными пришёл Саркар Тхакур, пришёл лучший из пандитов Кави Карнапура,
Шьямадас, Вишнудас, Шри Ядунандана и все остальные любимые ученики Адвайты.
Придя в Шантипур, все простёрлись у стоп Господа восемью частями тела и вознесли хвалу.
Господь сказал: «Вы все Мне дороже всего. Исполните по правде одно Моё слово:
достоинства и дхарму Шри Чайтаньи Махапрабху проповедуйте по мере сил — вот суть Моего сердца.
Общество всех безбожников и невеж, ненавидящих Шри Гаурангу, непременно следует оставить.
А теперь все вы, распевая киртан Гауре, исполните давнее желание Моего сердца».
Услышав это, все преданные исполнились любви и начали санкиртану имени и достоинств Гауры.
Шри Ачьюта, Кришнамишра, Гопала Тхакур, Господин Вирачандра, полный сладости Нарахари,
Гауридас Пандит и Дамодара Пандит — семеро плясали необычайно прекрасно.
Слушая о достоинствах Гауры, Господь исполнился любви и, войдя в санкиртану, стал плясать.
Волны океана санкиртаны поднимались всё выше, и Шри Адвайта погрузился в них в махабхаве.
Самоцветы оцепенения и прочих признаков украсили всё тело Господа, и Он заплакал: «Где Гора, жизнь Моя?»
Дивные чувства Господа невозможны для обычной души; окружив Господа, все преданные плакали от любви.
Тогда Господь сказал: «Вот Я обрёл Гаурангу!» — и тело Его стало подобно цветку кадамбы.
Внезапно Он вошёл в святой храм Мадана-Гопалы — и стал невидим для обычных людей.
Ища Господа, преданные бросились туда и сюда; не найдя Его, они плакали и катались в пыли.
Шри Ачьюта, поняв, что Шри Адвайта скрылся, громко плача, сказал всем спутникам Гауры:
«У древа желаний любви к Гауре оставался один ствол — потому сокрытие Гауры не было полным.
Ныне игры Гауранги завершились». Услышав это, все преданные непрестанно плакали.
«Ах, Гауранга! Ах, Гауранга! Ах, Нитьянанда! Слава воплощению преданного, Шри Адвайтачандре!» —
кроме этих слов, ничего не было на устах у всех; от этой скорби поистине таяли камни.
Прошли день и ночь — ни у кого не было внешнего сознания; на второй день все омылись в Ганге.
Господин Шри Ачьюта устроил великий праздник, и все, получив маха-прасад, разошлись по своим местам.
Сто двадцать пять лет Господь пребывал на земле и по порядку явил бесчисленное множество игр.
Этот океан нектара игр недоступен и неодолим: Ананта не находит ему конца — что уж я, ничтожный?
Ради очищения себя я дерзнул на это: я не смог коснуться и капли океана игр.

verses_en.text: Glory, glory to Sri Chaitanya! Glory to Sitanatha! Glory to Nityananda-Rama together with the devotees!
When Mahaprabhu had disappeared, the two Lords, overwhelmed by separation, wept.
The states I saw with my own eyes I, a worthless worm, am unable to describe.
As was the state of the gopis of Vraja without Krishna, so unceasingly was the state that manifested in both of Them.
Sometimes They fasted, sometimes They ate a little, sometimes They drank only water once in two or four days.
Their bodies, overpowered by separation, at times did not stir; at times They called out loudly, "Ah, Gauranga!"
A single day seemed to Them a hundred yugas; seeing the state of both, one's heart melted.
Their only joy within was the name of Gauranga. In this way the eighth year passed.
One day in Shantipura Sri Advaita Acharya, remembering the qualities of Gaura, lost all composure in prema.
At that time a letter came from Khardaha: Sri Nityananda had written asking the Acharya to come.
Receiving the letter, Sri Advaita set out in haste and arrived at Nityananda's abode.
At the auspicious meeting of Nityananda and Sri Advaita They embraced each other in great bliss.
Seeing each other, both were immersed in prema, and crying out "Gora!" They wept aloud.
After some time outer consciousness returned to both, and They sat together on one seat in seclusion.
Thus for seven nights the two sat in seclusion; what They spoke of, no one knows.
On the eighth day Sri Advaita, in great elation, sang kirtana of Gaura's qualities with the devotees.
In the midst Nityananda danced, beside Himself with prema, meditating on the lotus feet of Sri Gauranga.
All the mahantas in their prema forgot the outer world — and unnoticed Nityananda disappeared.
Coming back to themselves, all the mahantas, not seeing Nityananda, began to search for Him.
The Lord Advaita Ishvara, knower of all truth, understood that Sri Nityananda had become invisible.
Crying "Alas, alas!" He wandered about as if maddened with love: "Tell Me, why have You brought about such a calamity?
I am already half dead with grief of heart in the terrible separation from Gorachand.
Still I lived on, looking upon Your face. If You too have left — where shall I go now?"
Speaking thus and much more, the Lord lamented; not a drop of it could I write down.
Learning of Nityananda's disappearance, the devotees wept: "Where is Nityananda?"
Master Virabhadra, weeping, rolled in the dust, and Sri Advaitachandra consoled everyone.
He had preparations made for a great festival and sent invitations wherever the devotees were.
In due time all the mahantas came, and in Khardaha joy awoke once more.
On the day of the festival, having bathed, all together began a great sankirtana.
In seven groups fourteen madal drums resounded, and hundreds of sweet-sounding karatalas.
In each group one person danced, but the son of Kubera (Advaita) danced in all the groups.
As I saw that bliss of kirtana with my own eyes — so, for fear of length, I could not describe it.
After the sankirtana all the Sri Vaishnavas relished the sweetness of Gauranga's pastimes.
Then Master Virabhadra, having cleaned the place, carefully arranged three seats in one spot.
Setting out three offerings of food, he placed them there and began to speak to Sri Advaita:
"I will tell You one wish of mine: fulfil, Gosani, the desire of a child.
As formerly Mahaprabhu and the two Lords sat together and took Their meal,
so today take Your meal in my house — let these worthless eyes rejoice to see it."
All the mahantas agreed, saying, "Very well," and my Lord went to offer the food.
First He offered food to Sri Mahaprabhu, and on His right He placed Nityananda's offering;
on Gauranga's left the Lord Himself sat down. Seeing this, the Sri Vaishnavas raised the sound of Hari's name.
Master Virachandra performed the arati of the meal and, lighting incense and lamps, gazed upon the moonlike face.
With fresh love all the mahantas sang the kirtana of the arati of Gauranga's meal.
What that wondrous beauty was, the root of bliss, I cannot describe: my good fortune is small.
In the midst of the assembly Virabhadra raised his arms and said: "Hear one word of mine, all you Vaishnavas:
whoever holds a festival with a feast, let him likewise first offer food to the three Lords,
and afterwards carefully distribute that maha-prasada to sadhus, brahmanas and Vaishnavas.
By the meal of the three Lords the great sacrifice becomes complete; by the meal of the three Lords even the seat of honour is blessed.
Sri Chaitanya, Nityananda and Advaita Gosani — the three are one, and the one is three: They are not different.
Whoever sees a difference among the three will never attain the feet of Chaitanya.
Without Gaura's mercy one will not obtain loving devotion, and so rare a birth will pass in vain.
At whatever festival food is not offered to the three Lords, that person's sacrifice, like the sacrifice of Daksha, will not be completed.
He will not obtain the fruit of giving food: all will be ruined, the sacrifice will come to nothing,
and in the next world he will dwell in hell, and as long as the moon and sun shine he will find no release."
Hearing such words from Virachandra's lips, all the Vaishnavas said, "So be it! So be it!"
Then, after the meal, the Lord rose, rinsed His mouth and accepted betel.
Then Master Virabhadra joyfully distributed that maha-prasada.
All the brahmanas, Vaishnavas, sadhus, mahantas and others, receiving maha-prasada, felt their lives fulfilled.
After the festival Virachandra, receiving the Lord's order, joyfully prepared for the rite of offering (pashar).
In a new pot was curd mixed with turmeric, and on top fresh mango leaves made a lovely sight.
Covering it with a new cloth, he set it before Advaita.
At my Lord's order Sri Achyutananda performed the offering, joyfully singing kirtana.
Having performed the rite of auspicious curd (dadhi-mangala), all the associates of Sri Gauranga danced in the mood of the cowherds of Gokula.
The bliss that arose — I see no shore to it; for my own purification I write down only a particle of its essence.
After the festival the devotees went to their own places, and the Lord returned with us to Shantipura.
Back in His home the Lord was sorrowful: no other words were on His lips but "Hare Krishna."
One day I, a worm, at the Lord's order went to learn news of Navadvipa and came back to Shantipura.
I fell flat at the Lord's feet, and the Lord said, "Ishanadasa, tell the news."
I said: "The residents of Navadvipa are all deeply grieved at Gauranga's disappearance.
By good fortune I saw Damodara Pandita; he asked, 'Why have you come here?'
After Shachi-devi's disappearance Mother Vishnupriya, of her own will, had the devotees close the doors.
Without her permission no one may see her: she has taken upon herself an extremely severe vow.
At dawn, having bathed and performed the daily rites, she chants Hari's name, taking a little rice:
for each name she puts one grain of rice into a clay pot — thus she chants the name until the third watch of the day.
When her japa is finished, she takes only as many grains of rice as there were names, and carefully cooks them with her face covered by a cloth.
Without salt, without spices — she offers this rice to Mahaprabhu with pleading.
With many lamentations she gives water for rinsing the mouth, and she herself eats only a handful of the prasada.
The rest of the prasada she gives to the devotees. Who else could keep so severe a vow?'
Hearing these words, which fell like a thunderbolt, I thought: how can I have darshana of Mother?
At that time Gadadhara Dasa, Sri Rama Pandita and other eminent devotees came there.
All together with Damodara, to receive prasada, they entered the inner apartments with tears in their eyes.
Then, at Mother Vishnupriya's order, the Pandita took me, unworthy, into the inner apartments.
Going in, I saw that Mother's body was covered with a thick cloth; by the good fortune of millions of lives I saw only her holy feet.
By a particle of the devotees' mercy I received a little prasada: I felt my life fulfilled, and the sorrow left my heart.
What hardships Mother endures — what more can I say? Without superhuman power who could do such a thing?"
Hearing this, my Lord wept, but, accepting Krishna's will, He restrained His grief.
The state of Mother Vishnupriya that I saw with my own eyes — to tell it breaks my heart; I could not write it down.
Some days later Lord Sitanatha, sitting in the courtyard, was reading the Srimad-Bhagavatam.
At that time a pure Vaishnava came and bowed before the Lord with the eight limbs of his body.
The Lord asked him, "Where have you come from now?" He replied, "Lord, Virabhadra has sent me.
He is twenty years old, yet still uninitiated, for want of a worthy guru.
Therefore, hoping to receive mantra from You, he is coming here by boat, absorbed in prema."
The Lord said: "This decision of Vira's is not right: it goes against the consent of his own people.
Go and explain My words to Vira: let him receive mantra from Mother Jahnava."
Hearing this, the Sri Vaishnava went to Khardaha and conveyed the Lord's order to Jahnava.
Hearing it, Sri Jahnava sent a sadhu, brought Vira back and initiated him.
Now hear of the disappearance of Sri Advaita Prabhu — as I write of it, my heart breaks.
One day the Lord was seized by a great ecstasy and wandered about searching: "Where is Nimai?"
After a long while outer consciousness returned to the Acharya, and He called His beloved sons.
The Lord said: "Hear, My children, of My sorrow: wicked people of Mine blaspheme Gauranga.
My heart cannot bear this; in atonement for it I shall surely leave this body.
Therefore convey My order and bring here the dear devotees of Sri Gauranga."
Having said this, my Lord became motionless, and Sri Achyuta quickly sent the news everywhere.
Receiving the letter with the Lord's order, Master Virachandra came to Shantipura with the devotees.
From Ambika came Gauridasa Pandita; all the devotees of Navadvipa came to the Lord.
With his devotees came Sarkar Thakura; there came the best of panditas, Kavi Karnapura,
Shyamadasa, Vishnudasa, Sri Yadunandana and all the other beloved disciples of Advaita.
Arriving in Shantipura, all bowed at the Lord's feet with the eight limbs of their bodies and offered prayers.
The Lord said: "You are all most dear to Me. Faithfully carry out one word of Mine:
preach the qualities and the dharma of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu as far as you are able — this is the core of My heart.
The company of all the unbelievers and boors who hate Sri Gauranga must certainly be abandoned.
And now all of you, singing kirtana to Gaura, fulfil the long-cherished desire of My heart."
Hearing this, all the devotees were filled with prema and began sankirtana of Gaura's name and qualities.
Sri Achyuta, Krishna Mishra, Gopala Thakura, Master Virachandra, Narahari full of rasa,
Gauridasa Pandita and Damodara Pandita — these seven danced most beautifully.
Hearing of Gaura's qualities, the Lord overflowed with prema, entered the sankirtana and began to dance.
The waves of the ocean of sankirtana rose ever higher, and Sri Advaita sank into them in mahabhava.
The jewels of trembling stupor and the other ecstatic symptoms adorned the Lord's whole body, and He wept: "Where is Gora, My life?"
The Lord's wondrous emotions are impossible for an ordinary soul; surrounding the Lord, all the devotees wept with prema.
Then the Lord said, "Here, I have found Gauranga!" — and His body became like a kadamba flower.
Suddenly He entered the holy temple of Madana-Gopala — and became invisible to ordinary people.
Looking for the Lord, the devotees ran here and there; not finding Him, they wept and rolled in the dust.
Sri Achyuta, understanding that Sri Advaita had disappeared, weeping aloud, said to all of Gaura's associates:
"Of the wish-fulfilling tree of love for Gaura one trunk remained — therefore Gaura's disappearance was not complete.
Today the pastimes of Gauranga have come to their close." Hearing this, all the devotees wept without ceasing.
"Ah, Gauranga! Ah, Gauranga! Ah, Nityananda! Glory to the avatara as devotee, Sri Advaitachandra!" —
apart from these words nothing was on anyone's lips; from that grief even stones truly melted.
A day and a night passed with no one in outer consciousness; on the second day all bathed in the Ganga.
Master Sri Achyuta held a great festival, and all, receiving maha-prasada, went to their own places.
One hundred and twenty-five years the Lord remained on earth and in due order manifested countless pastimes.
That ocean of the nectar of His pastimes is inaccessible and uncrossable: Ananta finds no end to it — what then of me, worthless as I am?
For my own purification I have dared to do this: I could not touch even one drop of the ocean of His pastimes.
I have neither learning nor intelligence — how should I write a book? What I wished to write and what I have written, dharma is witness.
(My sources are) the sutras on the childhood pastimes (written by) Laudiya Krishnadasa — by reading that book the world is purified;
what I read and what I heard from Krishnadasa's lips, what Padmanabha and Shyamadasa told me;
the pastimes I saw with my own sinful eyes — all this, at the Lord's order, I have woven into a book.
In the year 1490 of the Shaka era I completed this book of pastimes in holy Lauda.
Why I came to holy Lauda — this confidential truth I shall tell the saintly briefly.
One day the Lord said to me in private: "My heart can no longer bear separation from Gauranga.
Soon I shall become invisible to the world of the living. Proclaim unceasingly Gaura's name and Gaura's qualities.
And I will tell you one thing more — listen attentively: you are My beloved disciple, like My own son.
When I am no longer seen, do not grieve: preach Gaura's name in My native land.
Faithfully carry out this order of Mine." Having said this, the Lord fell silent.
I think: if the order of the guru is carried out, then my birth and deeds will surely be fruitful.
After the Lord's disappearance Sita Thakurani — I do not know with what thought — gave me this order:
"O Ishanadasa, I love you dearly; I shall be pleased if you marry."
I said: "Mother, consider what you are ordering: to carry out this order is beyond my power.
I am nearly seventy years old — what brahmana would give me his daughter?"
Mother replied: "Krishna always fulfils His devotees' desires — that is why He is called the wish-fulfilling tree of the devotees.
Go east with Sri Jagadananda: he will take care to arrange your marriage.
There preach Gaura's name and dharma: by that many souls will be delivered.
Your descendants will become great bhagavatas and, giving the name of Hari, will set souls free."
Taking this order of Mother Sita upon my head, I came with Jagadananda Raya to the eastern country.
To continue the line and carry out the Lord's order, I came in haste to holy Lauda.
Living here, I wrote this book: I have only carried out the order of my guru.
I have written down only the essence, as I was ordered: let neither fault nor merit in it rest on me.
This is the alms I beg of the Vaishnavas who hear it: out of your own goodness forgive the offences of me, the lowly.
I am very old and have no knowledge at all: this book I have dedicated to the feet of Sri Chaitanya.
What was within my power, that I have written; may the sadhus in their kindness correct it.
The feet of guru, Krishna and the Vaishnavas are the essence of all: to the feet of them all I offer millions of obeisances.
These three are one reality in different forms: to deliver souls they manifest many forms,
— as in an earring and a necklace different shapes are seen, yet the cause is one, gold, and the soul perceives it.
These three are the sources of the avataras, oceans of mercy: the feet of these three are my boat across the ocean of worldly existence.
This is my prayer at the feet of these three: I am a great offender; my offences cannot be counted.
Out of Your own goodness pardon my offences — show forth Your name "Purifier of the fallen."
In all the three worlds there is none as fallen as I: may I at the end obtain a place at the reddish holy feet.

narottama-vilasa.title: Локанатха и Гопала Бхатта запрещают Кришнадасу Кавирадже писать о себе; шлоки о Локанатхе
narottama-vilasa.summary: Давая Кришнадасу Кавирадже позволение писать книгу, Локанатха запрещает описывать себя, так же поступает Гопала Бхатта; автор слышал это от старших; три шлоки во славу Локанатхи, милостивого к Нароттаме.

verses.text:
Когда Кришнадас Кавираджа попросил у Госвами
позволения написать книгу,

Госвами с радостью дал ему позволение,
но запретил описывать в ней его самого.

Когда тот пришёл за позволением к Шри Гопале Бхатте Госвами,
тот так же, с великим сокрушением, запретил ему.*
notes: Ср. ЧЧ: Кришнадас Кавираджа почти ничего не пишет о Локанатхе и Гопале Бхатте — по их собственной просьбе.

verses.text:
Эти рассказы я слышал из уст старших;
немного я описал их — удачливы те, кто это вкушает.

Локанатха Госвами безмерно милостив,
сосуд милости Шри Чайтаньи, полный драгоценной премы.

Он жил во Вриндаване всегда; кто постигнет его замысел?
С довольным сердцем он даровал милость Нароттаме.

Так сказано в шлоках:*
Тот, чьё единственное богатство — милость Кришна-Чайтаньи, чьё сердце богато золотыми украшениями премы к Нему, —
падая на землю, мы непрестанно склоняемся перед ним, Локанатхой Прабху, и принимаем у него прибежище.
notes: В изд. 1924 г. источник не назван; изд. 2021 г. относит эти шлоки к «Ставамрита-лахари» Вишванатхи Чакраварти (восьмистишие о Локанатхе).

verses.text:
Тот, кто обрёл вечное жительство во Вриндаване, в ком сияют игры и раса Кришны,
кто непрестанно и без отдыха следует своему благому укладу, — у него, Локанатхи Прабху, мы принимаем прибежище.
Чью силу милости познал великий мудрец по имени Нароттама,

verses_en.text:
When Krishnadasa Kaviraja asked the Gosvami
for permission to write his book,

the Gosvami gladly gave him permission,
but forbade him to describe himself in it.

When he went for permission to Sri Gopala Bhatta Gosvami,
he too, with great regret, forbade him in the same way.*
notes: Cf. the CC: Krishnadasa Kaviraja writes almost nothing about Lokanatha and Gopala Bhatta — at their own request.

verses_en.text:
These accounts I heard from the lips of the elders;
I have described a little — fortunate are those who relish it.

Lokanatha Gosvami is supremely merciful,
a vessel of Sri Chaitanya's mercy, full of the jewel of prema.

He lived ever in Vrindavana; who can fathom his intent?
With a pleased heart he bestowed his mercy on Narottama.

Thus in these verses:*
He whose only wealth is the mercy of Krishna-Chaitanya, whose heart is rich with the golden ornaments of prema for Him —
falling to the ground we bow to him constantly; we take shelter of him, Lokanatha Prabhu.
notes: The 1924 edition names no source; the 2021 edition ascribes these verses to Vishvanatha Chakravarti's Stavamrita-lahari (his octet on Lokanatha).

verses_en.text:
He who obtained eternal residence in Vrindavana, in whom Krishna's pastimes and rasa shine forth,
who follows his own good conduct ceaselessly and without rest — we take shelter of him, Lokanatha Prabhu.
Whose power of mercy the great sage named Narottama came to know,

bhakti-ratnakara.title: Гопала Бхатта и Локанатха запрещают Кришнадасу Кавирадже писать о себе
bhakti-ratnakara.summary: Гопала Бхатта, считая себя ничтожным, позволил Кришнадасу писать книгу, но запретил упоминать о себе, и Кавираджа назвал лишь его имя; то же повелел Локанатха (по словам старых вайшнавов); Гопала написал комментарий к «Кришна-карнамрите».

verses.text:
Шри Гопала Бхатта охотно дал позволение,
но запретил описывать в книге то, что касается его самого.

Почему запретил — кто поймёт?
Он всегда считал себя ничтожнейшим.

Кавираджа не мог нарушить его повеление:
он пишет лишь его имя, ничего иного не разглашая.

Такое же повеление дал и Локанатха Госвами;
это я слышал из уст старых вайшнавов*.
notes: О запрете Гопалы Бхатты и Локанатхи Госвами Кришнадасу Кавирадже писать о них — ср. «Према-виласу» и «Нароттама-виласу».

verses.text:
Другие кое-что описали в его отсутствие;
поистине необычайны достоинства этого Бхатты.

Игры учёности Бхатты во Вриндаване
из-за объёма книги я здесь не раскрыл.

Он написал комментарий к «Кришна-карнамрите»,
слушая который вайшнавы испытывают высшее блаженство.
Шри Гопала Бхатта, благородный на пути чистой бхакти,

verses_en.text:
Sri Gopala Bhatta gladly gave his permission,
but forbade him to describe in the book anything concerning himself.

Why he forbade it — who can understand?
He always considered himself the lowest of the low.

The Kaviraja could not transgress his order:
he writes only his name and makes nothing else known.

Lokanatha Gosvami too gave such an order;
this I heard from the lips of old Vaishnavas.*
notes: On the prohibition by Gopala Bhatta and Lokanatha Gosvami against Krishnadasa Kaviraja writing about them, cf. the Prema-vilasa and the Narottama-vilasa.

verses_en.text:
Others described a little of it in his absence;
truly extraordinary are the virtues of this Bhatta.

The Bhatta's play of learning in Vrindavana
I have not disclosed here because of the bulk of the book.

He wrote a commentary on the Krishna-karnamrita,
hearing which the Vaishnavas feel supreme bliss.
Sri Gopala Bhatta, noble on the path of pure bhakti,

bhakti-ratnakara.title: Род Рамачандры и Говинды Кавираджей: поэт Дамодара, Сунанда и Чиранджива
bhakti-ratnakara.summary: Дамодара Сена из Шрикханды, поэт, непобедимый в спорах, проклят дигвиджаи бессыновностью, но умилостивленный тот обещает дочь и двух внуков-драгоценностей; дочь Сунанда выходит за Чирандживу Сену из Кумаранагара, спутника Господа (ЧЧ Мадхья 11.92); рождается Рамачандра — «частица бога», явившийся в роду вайдьев.

verses.text:
Рамачандра и Шри Гокулананда — обители премы;
к слову расскажу здесь о них немного.

Рамачандра и Говинда — родные братья;
их отец — Чиранджива, дед по матери — Дамодара.

Дамодара Сена жил в Шрикханде;
его имя великого поэта известно миру.

Так [сказано] в драме Шри Говинды Кавираджи «Сангита-мадхава»:
«В Патале красноречив Васуки, на небесах красноречив Брихаспати; в Гауде щедр Говардхана, в Кханде — поэт Дамодара»*.
notes: Говардхана — по-видимому, землевладелец Говардхана Маджумдар, отец Рагхунатхи Даса Госвами, славный щедростью. Драма «Сангита-мадхава» приписывается Говинде Кавирадже (Говиндадасу), брату Рамачандры.

verses.text:
Поэт Дамодара был искусен в доводах;
никто никак не мог его одолеть.

Один дигвиджаи, легко побеждённый им,
в огорчении проклял его: «Будь бессыновен!»

Дамодара всячески его умилостивил,
и тот сказал: «У тебя будет дочь, благословенная в мире.

От неё родятся два сына-драгоценности;
их силой будет уничтожено всё неблагое».

У этого достойного брахмана родилась дочь по имени Сунанда*;
день ото дня она росла, благословенная красотой и достоинствами.
notes: В тексте — «випра-вара» («лучший из брахманов»), хотя род Дамодары Сены — вайдьи (см. 262); слово, видимо, употреблено в общем значении «почтенный муж».

verses.text:
Все женщины Кханды хвалят её;
когда она достигла брачного возраста, стали искать жениха.

Великий счастливец Дамодара Кавираджа
отдал дочь в жёны Чирандживе Сене.

В душе моей рождается страх перед объёмом книги,
поэтому свадебных торжеств я не могу описать подробно.

На берегу Бхагиратхи есть селение Кумаранагар;
там живут многие вайшнавы, прекрасное место.

В этом селении был дом Чирандживы Сены;
женившись, он поселился в Кханде.

Что скажу о жизни Чирандживы Сены?
Все жители Кханды считают его своей жизнью.

Мудрый спутник Шри Чайтаньи Прабху,
сердцем он всегда без ума от санкиртаны.

Чиранджива из Кханды известен повсюду:
бедных и сирых он сделал сосудами бхакти-расы.

В «Чайтанья-чаритамрите», говоря о встрече [преданных] с Господом,
упомянут Чиранджива Сена из Кханды.

Так [сказано] в «Чайтанья-чаритамрите»:
«Мукунда Дас, Нарахари, Шри Рагхунандана,
Чиранджива из Кханды и Сулочана»*.
notes: ЧЧ Мадхья 11.92.

verses.text:
Чиранджива Сена, во всём весьма сведущий,
живёт в Кханде со своей женой.

Жена его, верная мужу, подобна Арундхати,
нрава прекраснейшего, поступков необычайных.

Каковы отец и мать, таков и сын Рамачандра;
родившись, Рамачандра принёс великую радость.

С младенчества поведение его было пленительно;
мужчины и женщины видят в нём свою вторую жизнь.

Облик его исполнен великого сияния, красотой он — Мадана;
за короткое время он приобрёл большую учёность.

Глядя на Рамачандру, мудрые люди рассуждают:
«Это частица некоего бога, иначе и быть не может.
Он по своей воле явился в роду вайдьев,

verses_en.text:
Ramachandra and Sri Gokulananda are abodes of prema;
in passing I shall tell a little about them here.

Ramachandra and Govinda are brothers;
their father is Chiranjiva, their maternal grandfather Damodara.

Damodara Sena lived in Shrikhanda;
his name as a great poet is known to the world.

Thus [it is said] in Sri Govinda Kaviraja's drama Sangita-madhava:
"In Patala Vasuki is eloquent, in heaven Brihaspati is eloquent; in Gauda Govardhana is generous, in Khanda — Damodara the poet."*
notes: Govardhana is apparently the landholder Govardhana Majumdar, the father of Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami, famed for his generosity. The drama Sangita-madhava is attributed to Govinda Kaviraja (Govindadasa), Ramachandra's brother.

verses_en.text:
Damodara the poet was skilled in argument;
no one could get the better of him in any way.

A digvijayi, easily defeated by him,
in his chagrin cursed him: "Be without a son!"

Damodara appeased him in every way,
and he said: "You will have a daughter, blessed in the world.

From her two jewel-like sons will be born;
by their power all that is inauspicious will be destroyed."

To this worthy brahmana a daughter named Sunanda was born;*
day by day she grew, blessed with beauty and virtues.
notes: The text has "vipra-vara" ("best of brahmanas"), although Damodara Sena's family were vaidyas (see 262); the word seems to be used in the general sense of "worthy man".

verses_en.text:
All the women of Khanda praise her;
when she reached the age for marriage, they sought a bridegroom.

The greatly fortunate Damodara Kaviraja
gave his daughter in marriage to Chiranjiva Sena.

Fear of the bulk of the book arises in my mind,
so I cannot describe the wedding festivities in detail.

On the bank of the Bhagirathi is the village of Kumaranagara;
many Vaishnavas live there, a beautiful place.

In that village was the home of Chiranjiva Sena;
after his marriage he settled in Khanda.

What shall I say of the life of Chiranjiva Sena?
All the people of Khanda regard him as their very life.

A wise associate of Sri Chaitanya Prabhu,
his heart is ever mad with sankirtana.

Chiranjiva of Khanda is known everywhere:
he made the poor and lowly vessels of bhakti-rasa.

In the Chaitanya-charitamrita, where [the devotees'] meeting with the Lord is told,
Chiranjiva Sena of Khanda is mentioned.

Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-charitamrita:
"Mukunda Dasa, Narahari, Sri Raghunandana,
Chiranjiva of Khanda, and Sulochana."*
notes: CC Madhya 11.92.

verses_en.text:
Chiranjiva Sena, highly learned in every way,
lives in Khanda with his wife.

His wife, devoted to her husband, is like Arundhati,
of the finest character and extraordinary conduct.

As were the father and mother, so was the son Ramachandra;
by his birth Ramachandra brought great joy.

From infancy his conduct was captivating;
men and women see in him their second life.

His form is full of great splendour, in beauty he is Madana;
in a short time he acquired great learning.

Seeing Ramachandra, wise people reflect:
"This is a portion of some god; it cannot be otherwise.
By his own will he appeared in a family of vaidyas,

bhakti-ratnakara.title: Детство и учёба Шринивасы; мать учит его именам Гауры; любовь сельчан и преданных
bhakti-ratnakara.summary: Мать учит младенца произносить имена Гауры, Нитьянанды, Адвайты, Радхи и Кришны; в пять лет — начало учёбы, учитель Дхананджая Видья-вачаспати; чудакарана, шнур; быстрое овладение шастрами; старики хвалят его красоту; Говинда Гхош и другие рассказывают ему о Гауре.

verses.text:
Через некоторое время он ползает по двору;
видя эти забавы, все ликуют.

Держась за палец матери, он идёт ножками,
спотыкаясь, оглядывается по сторонам.

Отпустив палец матери, он падает на землю,
и мать, смеясь, скорее берёт его на руки.

Другие жёны брахманов, говоря ласковые слова,
берут его на руки и целуют прекрасное личико.

Так, передавая Шринивасу из рук в руки,
какую радость они испытывают — не рассказать.

Однажды Лакшмиприя с радостью в душе
говорит Шринивасе сладчайшими словами:

«Ну-ка, сынок, скажи: „Гаура Вишвамбхара,
супруг Лакшми и Вишнуприи, сын Шачи,

Господин жизни Гададхары, Владыка Шриваса,
Шри Кришна Чайтанья, Нитьянанда-Халадхара“.

Ну-ка, скажи: „Шри Адвайта Прабху милостивый“.
Ну-ка, скажи: „Радха-Кришна, сын Шри Нанды,

Говинда, Гопинатха, Мадана-мохан“», —
так она называет имена Господа и Его спутников.

Слыша это, Шриниваса в великой радости
что-то выговаривает, а что-то выговорить не может.

Услышав эти нектарные слова, утешив слух,
они с высшей радостью растят сына.

Шринивасе исполнилось пять лет;
он хочет учиться — слыша это, все рады.

Через некоторое время ему устроили начало обучения:
учёба — одно название, всё само раскрывается ему без труда.

Через некоторое время совершили чудакарану,
и дивно засиял на плече священный шнур.

За малое время он изучил грамматику, словари, поэтику,
логику и прочее — люди изумились.

Счастливец Дхананджая Видья-вачаспати
по мере сил передавал ему знания.

В Чакханди живёт много учёных людей,
и все они, видя Шринивасу, робеют.

Старые почтенные брахманы, преданные Вишну,
говорят друг другу: «Какое чудо!

За короткое время он постиг все шастры,
всегда безупречно чист и внимателен на пути бхакти.

Давно мы живём здесь,
но такого мальчика никогда не видели.

Какое тело — цвета чистого золота!
Как прекрасно лицо, как сладостна речь!

Когда он смеётся, сыплется нектар, зубы прекрасны;
как пленительны два длинных глаза!

Какой нос, уши, щёки, брови, лоб!
Какие гладкие вьющиеся прекрасные волосы!

Какой изгиб рук, какая красивая широкая грудь!
Несравненна прелесть живота, стан тонок.

Какие колени, голени, нежные стопы!
Разве у человека, не будь он частицей бога, бывает такое?

Шри Чайтанья Дас был бездетен —
и Господь дал ему сына, воплощение блаженства».

Кто-то говорит: «Взял бы я на себя его беды!
Не видя его, не знаю, что творится с сердцем, — не могу забыть».

Кто-то говорит: «В мирской жизни мы терпим великое горе,
а увидишь его — и в душе рождается счастье».

Кто-то говорит: «У меня много сыновей и дочерей,
но к Шринивасе любовь сильнее, чем к ним.

Как бы, под каким предлогом сказать Шри Чайтанье Дасу,
чтобы он поскорее его женил?»

Так, говоря друг с другом, они благословляют его;
в душе у них одно желание — всегда видеть его досыта.

Как Шриниваса родился в Чакханди и каков он —
всё это стало известно повсюду.

В дома преданных, живущих близ Чакханди,
Шриниваса постоянно ходит.

Шри Говинда Гхош и другие, потеряв от любви самообладание,
омывают его нектаром игр Шри Гаурачандры.

Как сказать, какую радость все испытывают?
Он хранит в сердце желание каждого.

Миг за мигом как дивно проявляется [их] любовь!
Все говорят: «Шриниваса — воплощение премы к Гауре».
Все повсюду рассказывают о Шринивасе,

verses_en.text:
After some time he crawls about the courtyard;
seeing his antics, everyone rejoices.

Holding his mother's finger, he walks on his little feet,
stumbling and looking all around.

Letting go of his mother's finger, he falls on the ground,
and his mother, laughing, quickly takes him in her arms.

Other brahmanas' wives, speaking affectionate words,
take him in their arms and kiss his lovely face.

So, passing Srinivasa from arm to arm,
what joy they feel cannot be told.

One day Lakshmipriya, joyful at heart,
says to Srinivasa in the sweetest words:

"Come, my son, say: 'Gaura Vishvambhara,
husband of Lakshmi and Vishnupriya, son of Shachi,

Lord of Gadadhara's life, Master of Srivasa,
Sri Krishna Chaitanya, Nityananda-Haladhara.'

Come, say: 'Sri Advaita Prabhu, the merciful.'
Come, say: 'Radha-Krishna, son of Sri Nanda,

Govinda, Gopinatha, Madanamohana'" —
so she says the names of the Lord and His associates.

Hearing this, Srinivasa in great joy
pronounces some and cannot pronounce others.

Hearing those nectarean words, their ears gladdened,
they raise their son in supreme joy.

Srinivasa reached five years of age;
he wants to study — hearing this, all are glad.

After some time they had his schooling begun:
study was in name only, everything revealed itself to him without effort.

After some time the chudakarana was performed,
and the sacred thread shone wondrously on his shoulder.

In a short time he studied grammar, lexicons, poetics,
logic and the rest — people were amazed.

The fortunate Dhananjaya Vidya-vachaspati
passed on knowledge to him as best he could.

In Chakhandi live many learned men,
and all of them grow shy on seeing Srinivasa.

The old venerable brahmanas devoted to Vishnu
say to one another: "What a wonder!

In a short time he has mastered all the shastras;
he is always spotlessly pure and careful on the path of bhakti.

We have lived here a long time,
but we have never seen such a boy.

What a body — the colour of pure gold!
How beautiful his face, how sweet his speech!

When he laughs nectar falls, his teeth are lovely;
how captivating are his two long eyes!

What a nose, what ears, cheeks, brows and forehead!
What glossy, curling, beautiful hair!

What a curve of the arms, what a handsome broad chest!
Incomparable is the charm of his waist, his middle is slender.

What knees, shanks and tender feet!
Can a human being, unless he is a portion of a god, be like this?

Sri Chaitanya Dasa was childless —
and the Lord gave him a son, the embodiment of bliss."

Someone says: "Would that I could take his troubles upon myself!
When I do not see him I know not what happens to my heart — I cannot forget him."

Someone says: "In worldly life we suffer great sorrow,
but when you see him happiness arises in the mind."

Someone says: "I have many sons and daughters,
but my love for Srinivasa is greater than for them.

On what pretext could I tell Sri Chaitanya Dasa
to get him married soon?"

So, speaking with one another, they bless him;
in their hearts is one desire — always to see their fill of him.

How Srinivasa was born in Chakhandi and what he is like —
all this became known everywhere.

To the houses of the devotees who live near Chakhandi
Srinivasa constantly goes.

Sri Govinda Ghosha and others, losing all composure out of love,
bathe him in the nectar of Sri Gaurachandra's pastimes.

How can I tell what joy they all feel?
He keeps in his heart the wish of each.

Moment by moment how wondrously [their] love shows itself!
All say: "Srinivasa is the embodiment of prema for Gaura."
Everyone everywhere talks of Srinivasa,

bhakti-ratnakara.title: Отец рассказывает Шринивасе об играх Господа; Чайтанья Дас собирается во Вриндаван
bhakti-ratnakara.summary: Шриниваса плачет, слушая; отец рассказывает о Нилачале, Нитьянанде, Адвайте, о Враджа-лиле и причине нисхождения; Шриниваса молит о сотнях тысяч ушей; отец, вверив ему мать, хочет уйти во Вриндаван и начинает рассказ о Рупе и Санатане.

verses.text:
Услышав этот рассказ из уст отца,
Шриниваса плачет в великом смятении.

Через некоторое время брахман Шри Чайтанья Дас
со вздохом повторяет: «Прекрасные вьющиеся волосы!»

С большим трудом овладев собой, он открывает глаза
и видит: сын плачет, упав на землю.

В упоении брахман берёт сына на колени
и благословляет: «Будь милостив к нему, Гаурахари!»

Стряхнув пыль с его тела и отерев слёзы,
он успокаивает его многими словами, подобными нектару.

С любовью он рассказал всё о том,
как увидел Господа в Нилачале.

Рассказывая, как Господь играет в Нилачале,
он проливает потоки слёз.

Он рассказал о жизни Нитьянанды и Адвайты,
поведал о жизни спутников Господа,

рассказал, как Господь играет во Врадже
и ради чего Он нисшёл в Навадвипе.

Слыша всё это из уст отца,
Шриниваса теряет самообладание, не может устоять на ногах.

Велико в душе желание слушать об играх Гауранги:
он молит Творца о сотнях тысяч ушей.

Глаза его, красные от любви, льют слёзы;
снова и снова он кланяется к стопам отца.

Забыв себя в экстазе премы,
Шриниваса изо дня в день расспрашивает отца.

Однажды почтенный брахман Шри Чайтанья Дас
говорит сыну с сердцем, полным любви:

«Сынок, ты стал способен заботиться о матери;
вместе с матерью я вверяю тебе всё.

Теперь, оставив тебя с матерью в Яджиграме,
думаю я поскорее уйти во Вриндаван.

Во Вриндаване через Рупу, Санатану и других
Прабху Гаура-рай совершил необычайные дела.

Сынок, жизнь этих двоих удивительна;
видя их, никак не подумаешь, что они люди.

Когда я видел их обоих,
у меня тогда такого понимания не было.
Теперь я считаю себя благословенным;

verses_en.text:
Hearing this account from his father's lips,
Srinivasa weeps in great distress.

After some time the brahmana Sri Chaitanya Dasa
sighs, repeating: "The beautiful curling hair!"

With great effort mastering himself, he opens his eyes
and sees: his son is weeping, fallen on the ground.

In rapture the brahmana takes his son on his lap
and blesses him: "Be merciful to him, Gaurahari!"

Brushing the dust from his body and wiping away his tears,
he calms him with many words like nectar.

Lovingly he told everything about
how he had seen the Lord in Nilachala.

Telling how the Lord plays in Nilachala,
he sheds streams of tears.

He told of the lives of Nityananda and Advaita,
he related the lives of the Lord's associates,

he told how the Lord plays in Vraja
and for what purpose He descended in Navadvipa.

Hearing all this from his father's lips,
Srinivasa loses his composure and cannot stand.

Great in his heart is the longing to hear of Gauranga's pastimes:
he begs the Creator for hundreds of thousands of ears.

His eyes, red with love, shed tears;
again and again he bows at his father's feet.

Forgetting himself in the rapture of prema,
Srinivasa questions his father day after day.

One day the venerable brahmana Sri Chaitanya Dasa
says to his son with a heart full of love:

"My son, you have become able to care for your mother;
together with your mother I entrust everything to you.

Now, leaving you with your mother in Yajigrama,
I am thinking of going soon to Vrindavana.

In Vrindavana, through Rupa, Sanatana and others,
Prabhu Gaura-raya accomplished extraordinary things.

My son, the lives of those two are wondrous;
seeing them, one could never think they are mere men.

When I saw the two of them,
at that time I did not have such understanding.
Now I consider myself blessed;

bhakti-ratnakara.title: Тоска отца и сына по Вриндавану; подпись и колофон
bhakti-ratnakara.summary: Чайтанья Дас мечтает уйти во Вриндаван, отец и сын плачут; слушающий их беседу обретает бхакти; подпись автора и колофон таранги.

verses.text:
О Шри Врадже я слышал из уст преданных;
это очень пространно — я рассказал тебе немного.

О Шриниваса, как томится душа!
Настанет ли такой день, когда я пойду во Вриндаван?»

Говоря так, Шри Чайтанья Дас
проливает потоки слёз и не может их унять.

Держась за стопы отца, плачет Шриниваса,
про себя говоря: «Исполнится ли моя надежда?»

Отец и сын успокоились лишь через некоторое время;
кто знает, сколь дивна мощь премы!

Кроме бесед о Кришне, ничто им не мило;
таким отцу и сыну не найти сравнения.

Кто слушает эту беседу отца и сына,
без труда обретает редчайшее богатство бхакти.
Размышляя о стопах Шринивасы Ачарьи,

verses_en.text:
Of Sri Vraja I have heard from the lips of devotees;
it is very extensive — I have told you a little.

O Srinivasa, how my soul longs!
Will there be such a day when I go to Vrindavana?"

Saying this, Sri Chaitanya Dasa
sheds streams of tears and cannot stop them.

Holding his father's feet, Srinivasa weeps,
saying to himself: "Will my hope be fulfilled?"

Father and son grew calm only after some time;
who knows how wondrous the might of prema is!

Apart from talk of Krishna nothing pleases them;
such a father and son have no comparison.

Whoever listens to this conversation of father and son
attains without effort the rarest wealth of bhakti.
Meditating on the feet of Srinivasa Acharya,

anuragavalli.title: Облик и юность Шринивасы; учёба и решение идти к Махапрабху в Нилачалу
anuragavalli.summary: Описание облика Шринивасы с головы до стоп (в зрелости он располнел); в отрочестве — грамматика, словесность, риторика, всё запоминал с одного прочтения; услышав о славе Махапрабху, решает идти в Нилачалу.

verses.text:
Теперь — лила Шринивасы Ачарьи Тхакура:
как он стал учеником Гопалы Бхатты, —

вкратце расскажу, лишь указав направление;
его стопы — моё единственное прибежище.

Махапрабху, Шри Кришна Чайтанья, источник аватар,
в последней лиле явно играл в Нилачале.

В ту пору родился Ачарья Тхакур.
Его облик в детстве и отрочестве был весьма сладостен.

В ранней юности — тело цвета чистого золота,
совершенство каждой части тела — какая обитель прелести!

Вьющиеся кудри, длинные лотосные глаза,
урдхва-тилака сверкает на лбу.

Блестящие брови, нос — как клюв попугая,
губы алые, зубы — ряды жемчуга.

Красивый подбородок, львиная шея, широкая полная грудь,
обвитая тончайшим священным шнуром.

Две руки — видеть их радость для сердца;
какой глупец сравнит их с хоботом царственного слона?

Ладони прекрасно-алые, пальцы плавно сужаются,
у всех — благие знаки, ногти — как драгоценные камни.
[с. 17]

Три складки на стане, тонкое тело;
бёдра, голени, плавно сужающиеся, колени прелестны.

Стопы — лепестки лотоса, ряды пальцев,
и на них сияют ногти блеском рубинов.

Он носил тонкую ткань, подвязанную тремя складками;
верхняя ткань украшает стройное тело.

Ожерелье из туласи — украшение шеи;
в руке — книга, поступь — как у упоённого царя слонов.

Таков был облик Тхакура вначале;
в средних летах он постепенно располнел.

В отрочестве, в течение нескольких дней, он начал учиться —
вошёл в грамматику, словесность и риторику.

Несказанная сладость его разума:
прочтя лишь раз, он запоминал наизусть.

Махапрабху явно играл в Нилачале;
услышав о беспредельной Его славе, (Шринивас) пришёл в волнение.

Он твёрдо решил в уме:
«Вскоре приму прибежище у стоп Махапрабху,

стану (Его), буду изучать „Шри Бхагавату“».
«Как это будет?» — эта мысль была непрестанной.

Ночью и днём росла так тоска;
решено было идти в Нилачалу.
Он сказал всем: «Я пойду в Нилачалу,

verses_en.text:
Now the pastime of Srinivasa Acharya Thakura:
how he became Gopala Bhatta's disciple —

I shall tell briefly, merely pointing the direction;
his feet are my only shelter.

Mahaprabhu, Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the source of avataras,
in His last pastimes was manifestly sporting in Nilachala.

At that time Acharya Thakura was born.
His form in childhood and boyhood was most sweet.

In early youth — a body the colour of pure gold,
the perfection of every limb — what an abode of loveliness!

Curling locks, long lotus eyes,
the urdhva-tilaka gleaming on his forehead.

Glossy brows, a nose like a parrot's beak,
red lips, teeth like rows of pearls.

A handsome chin, a lion's neck, a broad, full chest
encircled by the finest sacred thread.

Two arms — to see them is joy to the heart;
what fool would compare them to a royal elephant's trunk?

Palms beautifully red, fingers gracefully tapering,
all bearing auspicious marks, nails like jewels.
[p. 17]

Three folds at the waist, a slender body;
thighs and shanks gracefully tapering, charming knees.

Feet like lotus petals, rows of toes,
and on them the nails shine with the lustre of rubies.

He wore a fine cloth tied with three tucks;
the upper cloth adorns his shapely body.

A necklace of tulasi is the ornament of his neck;
a book in his hand, a gait like an intoxicated king of elephants.

Such was Thakura's form at first;
in middle age he gradually grew stout.

In boyhood, within a few days, he began his studies —
he entered grammar, literature and rhetoric.

The indescribable sweetness of his intellect:
reading a thing once, he knew it by heart.

Mahaprabhu was manifestly sporting in Nilachala;
hearing of His boundless glory, (Srinivasa) was deeply stirred.

He firmly resolved in his mind:
"Soon I shall take shelter at Mahaprabhu's feet,

become (His), and study the Sri Bhagavata."
"How will it come about?" — this thought was incessant.

Night and day his longing grew thus;
going to Nilachala was decided.
He told everyone, "I shall go to Nilachala

prema-vilasa.title: Аннапрашана и посвящение Шринивасы; перерыв в учении и сон о Вриндаване
prema-vilasa.summary: Родители растят сына; в благой день ему дают первый рис, затем совершают постриг и надевают священный шнур; на третий день мальчик плачет, что учение прервалось; пандит Видьянидхи радуется его рвению; во сне Шринивасу велят учиться быстрее — он пойдёт во Вриндаван, и через него Чайтанья явит в Гауде книги об играх.

verses.text:
Шесть месяцев Ачарья никуда не выходил из дому;
видя силу сына, он пребывал в покое.

Оба радовались, глядя на лицо сына,
и с лёгким сердцем растили его.

Пришло время аннапрашаны*;
пригласив астролога, твёрдо назначили день.
notes: Аннапрашана — первое кормление ребёнка рисом.

verses.text:
В благой миг вложили сыну в рот прасад,
и оба радовались, прижимая сына к груди.

Пришло время чуда-караны*;
совершив обряды по правилам, на него надели священный шнур.
notes: Чуда-карана — обряд первого пострига; священный шнур обычно надевают при упанаяне, но текст объединяет оба обряда.

verses.text:
Алое одеяние сияет на его теле;
глядя на него, отец и мать радуются в сердце.

На третий день Тхакур встревожился:
учение прервалось — он сидел дома и стал плакать*.
notes: После упанаяны юноша по обычаю несколько дней проводит в затворе и не ходит к учителю.

verses.text:
В это время пришёл пандит Видьянидхи*;
услышав о перерыве в учении, он очень обрадовался:
notes: Вариант: «пришёл Шри Рама Вачаспати».

verses.text:
«Так сильно стремится мальчик к знанию —
видно, Шринивас станет искусен в науках».

Однажды ночью Шринивасу приснилось:
«Учись быстрее, Шринивас, — ты пойдёшь во Вриндаван.

Гауда очень дорога Чайтанье;
через тебя Он явит здесь книги об играх.

Зачем ты три дня не учишься?
По слову родителей я буду тебя учить.
Если же ты поступишь вопреки этому слову,

verses_en.text:
For six months the Acharya did not go out anywhere;
seeing his son's power, he remained at peace.

Both rejoiced as they looked on their son's face,
and raised their son with happy hearts.

The time of the annaprashana* came;
they brought an astrologer and fixed the day firmly.
notes: Annaprashana, a child's first feeding with rice.

verses_en.text:
At an auspicious moment they put prasada into the son's mouth,
and both rejoiced, clasping their son to their breasts.

The time of the chudakarana* came;
performing the rites according to rule, they gave him the sacred thread.
notes: Chudakarana, the rite of the first tonsure; the sacred thread is normally given at the upanayana, but the text runs the two rites together.

verses_en.text:
A crimson cloth gleams upon his body;
seeing him, his father and mother rejoice at heart.

On the third day the Thakura grew restless:
his lessons had stopped — he stayed at home and began to weep.*
notes: After the upanayana a boy customarily spends some days in seclusion and does not go to his teacher.

verses_en.text:
At this time the pandit Vidyanidhi came by;*
hearing of the break in the lessons, he was greatly pleased:
notes: Variant: "Sri Rama Vachaspati came by".

verses_en.text:
"The boy has such a longing for learning —
it seems Srinivasa will become an expert in the sciences."

One night Srinivasa saw in a dream:
"Study quickly, Srinivasa — you will go to Vrindavana.

Gauda is very dear to Chaitanya;
through you He will make books of the pastimes arise here.

Why have you stopped studying for three days?
At your parents' word I will teach you.
But if you act against this word,

prema-vilasa.title: Учитель Дхананджая признаёт, что ученик превзошёл его; Сарасвати по повелению Чайтаньи дарует Шринивасу знание
prema-vilasa.summary: Мальчик непрестанно повторяет имя Радхи и Кришны и скорбит, что не станет пандитом; учитель Дхананджая Видьянивас говорит, что ученик похитил всю его учёность, и пристыженный Шринивас прячется дома с книгой; во сне ему является Сарасвати и по повелению Чайтаньи дарует всякое знание — с тех пор учение не прерывается.

verses.text:
Он постоянно произносил языком имя Радхи и Кришны,
а потому учение ушло — он не ходил учиться.

Лакшмиприя и Ачарья изумились:
не могли понять, что это за рождение*.
notes: В изд. 1913 г. это двустишие в скобках.

verses.text:
Он постоянно произносил языком имя Радхи и Кришны,
а потому учение ушло — но в сердце была радость.

Сидя дома, что говорит Шринивас?
«Я не стал пандитом» — вот какая боль у него на душе.

«Не могу постичь милости Кришны;
учёность даётся учением — таков её путь*.
notes: Вторая строка неясна; букв. «изучив, учёность его в таком поведении».

verses.text:
Поэтому не стану жить в Яджиграме:
ради учения уйду я в другие края».

Через десять дней мать велела ему:
«Ступай учиться, сынок, учение прервалось».

«Как велишь», — сказал он, взял в руки книгу,
и Шринивас пришёл к своему гуру.

Дхананджая Видьянивас сказал удивительное:
«Глядя на твой облик, я радуюсь.

Слушай, слушай, Шринивас, скажу тебе:
знание во мне больше не пробуждается — зачем ты пришёл?

Ты похитил всю мою учёность;
я — пустое тело, говорю тебе.

Не могу я понять твоей природы;
видно, Сарасвати отвернулась от меня».

Пристыженный, Шринивас поклонился гуру,
а Дхананджая в страхе вскочил, восклицая: «Увы, увы!»

Стыд Шринивасы особенно возрос, удвоившись;
удручённый, он завязал книгу и ушёл.

Отец и мать ничего этого не знали;
а он в горе от перерыва в учении лежал в уединении.

Обед был готов, а мальчика нет дома;
отец с тревогой в сердце пошёл его искать.

Пандит сказал: «Он давно ушёл».
Не найдя никакого следа, отец очень встревожился.

Войдя в дом, он прошёл в покой
и увидел, что тот спит с книгой в руке.

Услышав голос отца, тот от стыда ничего не сказал
и, проговорив: «Дай мне поесть, мама», — стал смеяться.
